'''Ivan Vladislavovich Sleshinsky<ref name="Schumann">Andrew Schumann. ''{{usurped|1=[https://web.archive.org/web/20160215232726/http://www.prastora.org/wp-content/uploads/2011/02/Logic-in-Central-and-Eastern-Europe2.pdf Logic in Central and Eastern Europe. The Social Context]}}'' 2012.</ref> or Jan Śleszyński'''<ref name="Schumann"/><ref>Storrs McCall. ''Polish Logic 1920-1939''. Oxford University Press. 1967. p. 13</ref><ref>Jan Woleński. ''Mathematical logic in Poland 1900-1939: people, circles, institutions, ideas''. Mod. Log. Volume 5, Number 4 (1995), pp. 367-368.</ref> ({{langx|ru|Иван Владиславович Слешинский}}) ({{small|Polish:}} {{IPAc-pl|ś|l|e|'|sz|y|ń|s|k|i}}; 23 July 1854 – 9 March 1931) was a Polish-Russian [[mathematician]]. He is regarded a pioneer of the study of [[logic]] in Poland.<ref name="FilKrak">{{cite web|url=https://filozoficznykrakow.wordpress.com/2015/01/20/jan-sleszynski-pionier-polskiej-logiki-w-krakowie/ |language=pl |title=Jan Sleszyński – pionier polskiej logiki w Krakowie |trans-title=Jan Śleszyński - A Pioneer of Logic in Kraków |website=filozoficznykrakow.wordpress.com |access-date=10 August 2026}}</ref> 

He worked as professor at the [[Odesa University]] and the [[Jagiellonian University]], and was the co-founder of the [[Polish Mathematical Society]]. His main areas of interest included [[continued fraction]]s, [[proof theory]] and [[mathematical logic]]. He is best known for introducing the [[Śleszyński-Pringsheim theorem]].

==Life and career==
Śleszyński was born on 23 July 1853 in [[Lysianka]], [[Russian Empire]] (present-day Ukraine) to Polish parents.<ref name="MacTut">{{cite web|url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Sleszynski/ |title=Ivan śleszyński |work=MacTutor History of Mathematics Archive |author=J.J. O'Connor, E.F. Robertson |access-date=10 August 2026}}</ref> In 1864, Śleszyński attended [[gymnasium (school)|gymnasium]] in [[Chișinău]]. After four years, he transferred to the A. Richelieu Gymnasium in [[Odesa]] finishing it with distinction.<ref name="Jadacki">{{cite web|url=https://www.ipsb.nina.gov.pl/a/biografia/jan-sleszynski-1854-1931-logik-matematyk-profesor-uniwersytetow |language=pl |title=Jan Sleszynski |website=ipsb.nina.gov.pl |author=Jacek Jadacki |access-date=10 August 2026}}</ref> 

He matriculated at the [[Odesa University]] to study mathematics, graduating in 1875. In 1880, after having received a scholarship, Śleszyński continued his studies attending lectures by [[Karl Weierstrass]] and [[Leopold Kronecker]] at the [[Humboldt University of Berlin|University of Berlin]]<ref name="Jadacki"></ref> where he earned his [[doctorate]] in 1882. Upon his return to Odesa, he was awarded the title of professor at his ''alma mater'', occupying the post from 1883 until 1909.<ref name="MacTut"></ref> He taught [[algebra]], [[number theory]], [[group theory]], the [[calculus of variations]], and the theory of [[analytic function]]s at the university. At the same time, he worked as a mathematics teacher at a local theological seminary, secondary schools in Odesa, and at the Higher Women’s Courses.<ref name="Jadacki"></ref> In the 1890s, Śleszyński became a leading figure among the mathematicians in Odesa influencing such scholars as [[Samuil Shatunovsky]] and [[Benjamin Kagan]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://fs.onu.edu.ua/clients/client11/web11/litopis/Sleshinskiy.pdf |title=Sleshinskyi Ivan Vladyslavovych |language=uk |work=Odesa University Chronicle |date=1 October 2024 |access-date=10 August 2026}}</ref>

In 1909, the publication of Śleszyński's translation of [[Louis Couturat]]'s book ''The Algebra of Logic'' was released. His version went well beyond a simple translation as it was enriched with his own valuable commentary exerting a substantial impact on the development of [[mathematical logic]] in Russia and serving for many years as the principal textbook for students of the field.<ref name="MacTut"></ref> 

In 1911, he moved to Poland, where he became "extraordinary professor" at the [[Jagiellonian University]] in [[Kraków]]. Among his notable students was [[Stanisław Zaremba (mathematician)|Stanisław Zaremba]]. In 1919, Śleszyński was one of the founding members of the [[Polish Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ptm.org.pl/zawartosc/polskie-towarzystwo-matematyczne-w-latach-1919-1963?utm_source=copilot.com |language=pl |title=Polskie Towarzystwo Matematyczne w latach 1919-1963 |trans-title=The Polish Mathematical Society in 1919-1963 |website=ptm.org.pl |access-date=10 August 2026}}</ref> In the same year, he was appointed full Professor of Logic and Mathematics lecturing at the university until his retirement in 1924.<ref name="MacTut"></ref> In 1925, he received the title of an honorary professor of the Jagiellonian University.<ref name="Jadacki"></ref> He was a member of the Kraków Philosophical Society ([[polish language|Polish]]: ''Towarzystwo Filozoficzne w Krakowie'').<ref name="FilKrak"></ref>

He died on 9 March 1931 in Kraków<ref name="MacTut"></ref> and was buried at the [[Rakowicki Cemetery]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://in-memoriam.uj.edu.pl/komitet/odnowione-groby |language=pl |title=Mogiły odrestaurowane staraniem Komitetu ds. Opieki nad Grobami Profesorów UJ (w porządku chronologicznym ich odnawiania) |trans-title=Graves restored through the efforts of the Committee for the Care of UJ Professors’ Tombs (in the chronological order of their restoration) |work=Jagiellonian University |access-date=10 August 2026}}</ref>

===Contributions===
In his 1892 paper, based on his doctoral thesis, Śleszyński revisited [[Augustin-Louis Cauchy|Cauchy]]’s formulation of the [[Central limit theorem]] applying characteristic functions, and introducing several important corrections and refinements.<ref name="MacTut"></ref>

Śleszyński's main work was on [[continued fraction]]s, [[least squares]] and axiomatic [[proof theory]] based on [[mathematical logic]]. He and [[Alfred Pringsheim]],<ref>{{cite journal|jfm=29.0178.02|last=Pringsheim|first=A.|title=Ueber die Convergenz unendlicher Kettenbrüche|language=German|journal=Münch. Ber.|volume=28|pages=295&ndash;324|year=1898}}</ref> working separately, proved what is now called the [[Śleszyński–Pringsheim theorem]].<ref>{{cite journal|last=Слешинскій|first=И. В.|title=Дополненiе къ замѣткѣ о сходимости непрерывныхъ дробей|journal=Матем. Сб.|volume=14|issue=3|year=1889|pages=436&ndash;438|url=http://mi.mathnet.ru/msb7210|language=Russian}}</ref>

Śleszyński upheld the autonomy of logic with respect to mathematics, arguing that logic cannot be reduced to a mere methodological instrument of mathematical practice.<ref name="FilKrak"></ref>

His most important publications include: ''Teoria dowodu'' (The theory of proof) in two volumes (1925, 1929), and ''Teoria wyznaczników'' (The theory of determinants) (1926).<ref>P. S. Krzystek. ''"Teoria dowodu" Jana Śleszyńskiego''. Ruch filozoficzny. Vol. 33. n. 3/4. 1975. Polskie Towarzystwo Filozoficzne. p. 338.</ref>
